title: Tempered Distributions and the Fourier Transform

items.title: Tempered distribution
items.strategy: Use seminorm topology, with continuity equivalent to sequential continuity because S is metrizable.
items.statement: S prime(R^n) is the continuous complex-linear dual of S(R^n), with bilinear distribution pairing.

items.title: Finite seminorm bound characterizes tempered distributions
items.strategy: A continuous functional is bounded on a finite intersection of seminorm balls; scale. Conversely the finite bound proves continuity.
items.statement: u is tempered iff |u(phi)|<=C max_{|alpha|<=N,|beta|<=M} sup_x |x^alpha partial^beta phi| for some C,N,M.

items.title: Weak and strong topologies on tempered distributions
items.strategy: The finite-seminorm bound makes the strong dual seminorms finite. Singleton bounded sets prove strong implies weak.
items.statement: Weak topology is pointwise on S; strong topology is uniform on bounded subsets of S, where bounded means bounded in every Schwartz seminorm.

items.title: Polynomial growth functions define tempered distributions
items.strategy: Bound the integral by the weighted L1 norm times a Schwartz seminorm. Use Holder with a sufficiently integrable inverse polynomial weight for Lp. Pointwise growth is sufficient, not a necessary characterization of regular tempered distributions. For n>=1 include the radial calculation for the function |x|^p away from zero, assigning any finite value at zero when p<0: local integrability at zero requires p>-n, and an inverse polynomial weight makes the tail integrable.
items.statement: If a real- or complex-valued locally integrable f satisfies integral |f(x)|(1+|x|)^(-N) dx<infinity for some N, then its regular distribution is tempered. This includes functions of pointwise polynomial growth outside a compact set and every Lp class for 1<=p<=infinity.

items.title: Fourier transform of a tempered distribution
items.strategy: Transpose the Schwartz transform using the bilinear pairing; no complex conjugation or inverse transform in the defining pairing. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: Define <Fu,phi>=<u,Fphi> with Fphi(xi)=integral phi(x)exp(-2 pi i x.xi) dx.

items.title: Fourier transform on tempered distributions is well defined and continuous
items.strategy: Apply continuity on S, and bounded-set preservation for the strong dual. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: The Fourier transform on S prime is well-defined and continuous in weak and strong dual topologies.

items.title: Fourier transform is a topological automorphism of tempered distributions
items.strategy: Transpose the inverse and reflection identities from S directly, avoiding any reliance on unproved density of S in S prime. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: Fourier transform is an automorphism in both dual topologies; F^2 u=Ru, Ru(phi)=u(phi(-.)), and F^{-1}=RF.

items.title: Fourier transform agrees with l one and plancherel transforms
items.strategy: L1 agreement uses absolute Fubini. Approximate L2 functions by Schwartz functions, use Cauchy-Schwarz on each test pairing and the unitary extension, and pass to the limit. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: For f in L1, Fu_f=u_{integral Fourier f}; for f in L2, Fu_f=u_{Plancherel f}.

items.title: Convolution of a tempered distribution with a schwartz function
items.strategy: Translation and reflection keep the test Schwartz; this initially defines a scalar function.
items.statement: For u tempered and phi Schwartz define (u*phi)(x)=<u(y),phi(x-y)>.

items.title: Dirac comb
items.strategy: Choose an integer decay order N>n+1. The lattice points with m<=|k|<m+1 are at most (2m+3)^n, so the weighted lattice sum is dominated by a convergent real p-series; this bounds the absolute sum by one Schwartz seminorm. On D the sum is locally finite.
items.statement: The Dirac comb III=sum_{k in Z^n} delta_k acts on Schwartz tests by their absolutely convergent lattice sum.

items.title: Dirac comb is fourier invariant
items.strategy: Pair with an arbitrary Schwartz test and apply the earlier A-page Poisson summation theorem, not its Gaussian B example. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: F III=III under the 2 pi normalization.

items.title: Test function inclusion in schwartz space is continuous
items.statement: The inclusion D(R^n)->S(R^n) is continuous with dense image.
items.strategy: On each D_K polynomial weights are bounded; use the LF universal property for continuity and the earlier Schwartz cutoff-density lemma for density. Density alone does not establish continuity.

items.title: Compactly supported distributions are tempered
items.strategy: Use the fixed cutoff and global finite-order estimate; uniqueness follows from D density in S. Compatibility with the D prime restriction is explicit.
items.statement: Every compactly supported distribution on R^n extends uniquely to a tempered distribution.

items.title: Tempered distributions embed continuously in distributions
items.strategy: Continuity of D->S sends bounded subsets to bounded subsets; transpose is continuous. Density makes the transpose injective. Do not claim a topological embedding onto its image.
items.statement: Restriction gives a continuous injection S prime->D prime for weak and strong topologies.

items.title: Smooth polynomially bounded multipliers on schwartz space
items.statement: If a is smooth and every derivative has some polynomial growth bound, multiplication by a is continuous S->S and hence on both dual topologies by transpose.
items.strategy: Expand derivatives by Leibniz and dominate each output seminorm by finitely many higher input seminorms. Polynomial multipliers and Schwartz multipliers are special cases; arbitrary smooth functions are not. For the dual assertion, transpose this continuous Schwartz operator and check bounded-set images for the strong topology.

items.title: Differentiation and polynomial multiplication preserve tempered distributions
items.strategy: Transpose the corresponding continuous operators on S, including the distributional derivative sign, and verify agreement with the already-defined D-prime derivative and smooth-multiplier operations after restriction. Continuous Schwartz operators send bounded sets to bounded sets, giving strong continuity.
items.statement: Differentiation and polynomial multiplication preserve S prime and are continuous weakly and strongly.

items.title: Fourier differentiation and multiplication identities on tempered distributions
items.strategy: Test each first-order identity and iterate, keeping the distribution derivative sign. Plane waves test the frequency sign. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: F(partial^alpha u)=(2 pi i xi)^alpha Fu and F(x^alpha u)=(-1/(2 pi i))^|alpha| partial_xi^alpha Fu.

items.title: Fourier transform of delta constants plane waves and polynomials
items.strategy: Evaluate the defining pairing at a; apply Schwartz inversion at zero; modulation and derivative identities give the remaining formulas. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: F delta_a=exp(-2 pi i a.xi), F1=delta_0, F exp(2 pi i b.x)=delta_b; F(partial^alpha delta_0)=(2 pi i xi)^alpha and F(x^alpha)=(-1/(2 pi i))^|alpha| partial^alpha delta_0.

items.title: Constant coefficient differential operators become polynomial multipliers
items.strategy: Use linearity and the derivative identity. Supply only algebraic equivalence, no general division, existence or regularity theorem. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: For P(partial)=sum a_alpha partial^alpha, F(P(partial)u)=P(2 pi i xi) Fu in S prime.

items.title: Schwartz parameter pairing and integral interchange
items.statement: Translations of a Schwartz test are smooth in every Schwartz seminorm. Assuming Countable Choice, if all needed parameter integrals are dominated in every seminorm, a tempered distribution commutes with the Lebesgue integral; the translation-smoothness clause itself holds in ZF.
items.strategy: Use Taylor integral remainders with polynomial weights; for integration approximate on compact parameter boxes by Riemann sums and control tails in every seminorm. State these estimates explicitly for each use, avoiding an unproved vector-valued integration theorem. Countable Choice is used only to supply the published Lebesgue integration interface for the integral-interchange clause.

items.title: Tempered convolution is smooth with polynomial growth
items.strategy: Apply the finite-seminorm bound directly to translated tests and use weighted Taylor remainders in Schwartz seminorms to differentiate the scalar pairing. Polynomial growth then invokes the regular-tempered criterion; no parameter integral is needed.
items.statement: u*phi is smooth, every derivative has polynomial growth, and partial^alpha(u*phi)=(partial^alpha u)*phi=u*(partial^alpha phi).

items.title: Fourier transform of a compactly supported distribution is a smooth polynomially bounded multiplier
items.statement: For compactly supported v, Fv(xi)=<v(x),chi(x)exp(-2 pi i x.xi)> is smooth, independent of chi, and every derivative is polynomially bounded.
items.strategy: The compact finite-order estimate bounds every xi derivative by C_alpha(1+|xi|)^m. Commuting the compactly supported distribution pairing with the rapidly convergent Fourier integral identifies this function with Fv. Countable Choice is used for the published Lebesgue Fourier-integral and parameter-interchange clauses; the compact finite-order estimate itself is choice-free.

items.title: Compact distribution convolution preserves schwartz and tempered spaces
items.statement: If v has compact support then phi->v*phi maps S continuously to S. For u tempered, u*v is tempered and agrees with the D prime convolution.
items.strategy: Keep the compact support of v fixed and bound weighted derivatives of phi(x-y) uniformly over y in a compact neighborhood. Transpose the reflected convolution operator to S prime and check agreement on compactly supported tests. Only the ZF smooth-parameter clause of the published distribution-pairing lemma is used; its integral-interchange clause is not used.

items.title: Fourier transform converts allowed tempered convolutions to products
items.strategy: For the Schwartz case commute the pairing with a seminorm-dominated integral and use the Schwartz convolution identity. For compact support, Fv is a smooth multiplier and v preserves S under convolution; test and interchange the compact-support pairing. No product of two arbitrary distributions is used. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: F(u*phi)=(Fu)(Fphi) for u in S prime, phi in S; F(u*v)=(Fu)(Fv) for u in S prime and compactly supported v. Also F(phi u)=(Fphi)*(Fu).

title: Tempered Distributions and the Fourier Transform — Examples

items.title: Fourier transform of dirac and one
items.strategy: Evaluate against a Schwartz test and use inversion at zero. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: F delta_0=1 and F1=delta_0.

items.title: Fourier transform of a plane wave
items.strategy: Use modulation with the negative-sign Fourier transform. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: F exp(2 pi i b.x)=delta_b.

items.title: Fourier transform of delta derivatives and monomials
items.strategy: Compute the pairings including the minus sign in the derivative of delta. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: F(delta_0 prime)=2 pi i xi and Fx=-(2 pi i)^(-1)delta_0 prime on R.

items.title: Principal value one over x is tempered and its fourier transform
items.strategy: Reprove the principal-value bound on S directly so no B-page dependency is needed. Use x pv(1/x)=1 to get D Fpv=-2 pi i delta; derivative of sgn is 2 delta. The difference is constant and oddness forces zero; need continuity of reflection and the zero-derivative theorem. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: pv(1/x) is tempered and its Fourier transform is -i pi sgn(xi).

items.title: Dirac comb and poisson summation
items.strategy: Evaluate on a Gaussian and on a general Schwartz test; the latter is Poisson summation. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: The unit lattice comb is Fourier invariant.

items.title: Fundamental solution by division of a fourier symbol
items.strategy: Directly compute the integrable Fourier transform and multiply its symbol; Fourier injectivity proves the equation. This is a B example, not a PDE prerequisite. Assume Countable Choice exactly for the cited published Fourier or Lebesgue-integration interface; the formal transpose and algebraic reduction add no stronger choice.
items.statement: On R, E(x)=exp(-|x|)/2 satisfies (1-D^2)E=delta_0 and FE=1/(1+4 pi^2 xi^2).

items.title: Product of two distributions is not canonically defined
items.strategy: First realize H=1_(0,infinity) as a regular distribution and prove DH=delta_0 by complex integration by parts; Countable Choice is used only for that published Lebesgue interface. In the proposed algebra H^2=H implies 2H delta=delta, while H^3=H gives 3H^2 delta=delta. Associativity then yields delta=0, contradicting injectivity. This is a precisely stated obstruction, not a claim that no special distribution products exist.
items.statement: No associative commutative differential algebra extending all pointwise products of piecewise smooth functions can simultaneously retain the distribution derivative and an injective embedding of these distributions.

items.title: Convolution of two tempered distributions need not exist
items.strategy: The addition-pullback integral of a nonnegative test of positive mass diverges; the fibers have infinite volume. No claim is made about separately chosen regularizations.
items.statement: The ordinary convolution of the two tempered constant distributions 1 and 1 is undefined.

items.title: Paley wiener and microlocal analysis
items.strategy: Orientation only. No recorded unproved theorem is promoted to a supplier.
items.statement: Paley-Wiener theory and microlocal analysis lie beyond this foundational pair.
